question.problem:
The systolic blood pressure of a group of people is normally distributed with a mean of $\mu \,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}$ and a standard deviation of $14\,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}.$ Additionally, $60%$ of the people have a systolic blood pressure between $0.9\mu \,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}$ and $1.1\mu \,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}.$ Find the percentage of people with a systolic blood pressure lower than $110\,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}.$

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ | $\,0.97\,$ | $\,0.99\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ |

$$

$$

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.6\,$ | $\,0.2578\,$ | $\,0.2546\,$ | $\,0.2514\,$ |
| $\,-0.5\,$ | $\,0.2912\,$ | $\,0.2877\,$ | $\,0.2843\,$ |
| $\,-0.4\,$ | $\,0.3264\,$ | $\,0.3228\,$ | $\,0.3192\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the systolic blood pressure of a randomly selected person. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{14}^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X<110).$ But first, we need to find the mean $\mu .$ 

We know that $P(0.9\mu <X<1.1\mu )=0.6.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.9\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.6 \\ 2P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.6 \\ P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.3 \\ P(X<\mu )+P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.5+0.3 \\ P(X<1.1\mu ) & =0.8\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.1\mu ) & =0.8 \\ P(Z<\frac{0.1\mu }{14}) & =0.8 \\ Φ(\frac{0.1\mu }{14}) & =0.8 \\ \frac{0.1\mu }{14} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.8)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.8)≈0.8416.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{0.1\mu }{14} & =0.8416 \\ 0.1\mu  & =11.7824 \\ \mu  & =\frac{11.7824}{0.1} \\  & ≈117.824.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(X<110)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<110) & =P(Z<\frac{110-117.824}{14}) \\  & ≈P(Z<-0.56) \\  & =Φ(-0.56) \\  & =0.2877 \\  & ≈28.8%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $28.8%$ of the people have a systolic blood pressure lower than $110\,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}.$
